title: Getting into the GA4 demo account
body_md:
## What the demo account is

Google's GA4 demo account is free for anyone with a Google account. It holds two properties:

- **Google Merchandise Store**: web data from Google's online merchandise shop. Every lab here uses it.
- **Flood-It!**: app and web data from a game.

The data is real, but obfuscated, and it changes every day.

## Getting access

- Sign in to the Google account you want to use.
- Open the Analytics Help article "Demo account" (support.google.com/analytics/answer/6367342) and click either property link.
- If you already have Google Analytics, the demo account is added to it. If not, Google creates an Analytics account for you and adds the demo to it.
- In Google Analytics, open the account selector (top left) and choose Demo Account > Google Merchandise Store or Flood-It!.

Keep the app and Google Analytics open side by side, in two tabs or two windows.

## What Viewer access allows

Everyone gets the Viewer role. You can:

- see every standard report and Realtime;
- read the settings in Admin (data streams, events, key events, data retention, attribution settings), but not change them;
- filter tables, add secondary dimensions and comparisons, and apply segments;
- build personal explorations (Free form, Funnel, Path and others). A lab may ask for one; it changes nothing in the property.

You cannot:

- export a report or an exploration (no PDF, CSV or Sheets);
- change any configuration: mark key events, create or edit events, audiences or custom definitions, or change attribution or retention settings;
- use the User exploration technique, the device ID dimension or the Analytics Data API.

So every lab asks you to find and read something, or to build a personal exploration, never to change the property.

## Menu paths

Some menu paths in the labs are not confirmed yet, and the lab says so. If your menu differs, use the search bar at the top of Google Analytics. Report paths start at Reports > Life cycle; a newer property may show a Business objectives collection instead, but the Merchandise Store should have Life cycle.

## How your answers are checked

The demo data changes every day, so the app stores no right numbers to compare yours with. Each part of a lab is checked in one of four ways:

- **Facts about GA4**, such as where a menu is or what a setting means, have one right answer.
- **Values from one screen** must fit together. For example, engaged sessions divided by sessions must give the engagement rate you read.
- **A re-check a week later**: you read the same value again, on the same month or the same dates. It should come out nearly the same. Small drift is allowed: 2% for users and sessions, 1% for event counts. Names and settings must match exactly.
- **A self-check**: you compare your screen with a description of what it should show.

A lab with a fixed month uses the month the app shows. A Last 28 days lab asks you to type the dates GA4 shows, and the re-check uses those same dates.

## Removing it later

To remove the demo account, open a demo property, then go to Admin > Account access management > Remove myself.
